note: THE COMPONENT CATALOGUE — what a customer may put on a payslip, and which side of it. It arrived as a 25-entry object literal inside the configuration screen's JavaScript, which is a business list living in code twice over: in code, and in the ONE file a customer never edits. A customer who calls their conveyance allowance something else, or who has a component this list has never heard of, would have needed a release. Here it is a file. `kind` decides which side of the payslip a component lands on and is not a label: an earning added to the deductions column is a payslip that adds up and is wrong.

kinds.earning: Paid to the employee and shown in the earnings column.
kinds.deduction: Taken from the employee's pay and shown in the deductions column.
kinds.employer_cost: Paid by the employer ON TOP of the salary. It never reduces net pay and it is never an earning — showing it in either column overstates one of them, which is how a CTC letter and a payslip come to disagree by exactly the employer's PF contribution.

government.source: Code on Wages 2019 s.2(y), in force 21-11-2025: wages (Basic + DA + retaining allowance) must be at least 50% of total remuneration, so Basic is 50% of Gross when there is no DA.

components.label: Overtime Pay
components.note: The only component whose formula may use # Hours, and the only one that carries a Max OT hours cap. The cap is here rather than in the screen because 'we allow thirty overtime hours a month' is a policy somebody sets.

statutory_note: A component marked `statutory` is one whose RATE is law, not policy. This build computes none of them: config/statutory is a synthetic pack whose figures are machinery evidence and state no law, and nothing here invents a PF, ESI, PT or gratuity rate. Marking them is what lets the screen say so on the row rather than letting somebody type 12% into a field and believe the product agrees with them.

calculations.label: % OF
calculations.note: A percentage of CTC or of Basic. The basis is asked for rather than assumed, because '40% HRA' means two different amounts depending on which it is of and every customer means a different one.

calculations.label: Monthly
calculations.note: A flat amount stated per month. Kept apart from Flat because a flat figure on an annual structure and a flat figure per month differ by twelve, which is the exact defect that made every payslip in this product twelve times too high once already.

calculations.label: Manual calculation
calculations.note: Computed as N IF conditions, each with its own calculation, checked in order, plus a default ELSE calculation (owner request, 12 Sep 2026, widened same day to n conditions with n calculations and comparison/conditional operators). Add at least one condition on the Salary Structure screen. A plain term-by-term formula with no condition is not yet computed.

calculations.label: Balance
calculations.note: Whatever is left of the gross after every other component. Exactly one component may be the balance — two of them is an unsolvable structure, and the screen refuses it.

calculations.label: Employee Gender
calculations.note: A treatment per gender (Male, Female, Other / not set): Exempt, Flat amount, % of Gross/Basic, or As per Government rules (owner request, 13 Oct 2026). E.g. Professional Tax exempt for women.

calculations.label: Same as
calculations.note: Offered only on a component that names its pair with "same_as" (Provident Fund (Employer) -> Provident Fund (Employee)). The employee's own winning rule for the pair is used as-is, so slabs, percentages and criteria are set once (owner request, 16 Oct 2026).

status_note: Each of these is a REAL COLUMN on `employees`, named here so a rule cannot be written against a field the table does not have. That check is the difference between a deduction that applies to nobody and a deduction that applies to nobody VISIBLY.

system_values.label: Number of calendar days in month
Number of working days in month

system_values_note: Calendar days and working days give different answers for the same month and the same attendance, which is why config/calendar.json makes the proration basis a declared choice. Offering both here is deliberate: a formula that says which one it means is one somebody can argue with.
